headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Planning a Complete Bathroom Renovation
articleBody:
A full bathroom renovation transforms everyday living, but small oversights during initial planning can trigger costly rework. Steer clear of these common pitfalls when updating your bathroom.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:
1. Treating tile and grout as waterproof barriers. Grout and tile absorb water over time; always install a verified sheet or liquid waterproofing membrane behind the tile.
2. Commencing demolition before pulling permits. Major plumbing, structural, and electrical changes require local building review before walls are opened.
3. Overlooking dedicated exhaust ducting. Depending solely on a window can trap humidity; verify that your mechanical fan vents fully to the home's exterior.
4. Finalizing fixture orders late. Waiting to buy valves and vanities can stall the rough-in schedule and delay wall closures.
5. Skipping shower pan testing. Neglecting a proper flood test on a custom mud bed can lead to leaks underneath finished flooring.

What Can Change the Right Choice:
Your home's framing and existing plumbing drop locations dictate whether moving fixtures makes practical sense. Working with licensed trades prevents costly framing alterations.
